subject: Soft failover / circuit plan — BrightCart latency surge & standby
messages:
From: Samuel Lee <sam@brightcart.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightCart SRE Team <ops@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: High tail latency starting ~08:45 PDT — can we get a standby plan?

Rishi,

We started seeing p95/p99 for our checkout embed jump around 08:45 PDT — tail latency to 1.8s (baseline ~450ms). Traffic is steady but token sizes are up; customers are complaining about UX. Can Redwood give us a quick mitigation plan we can standby for (fallback model, rate-limit guidance, or other)? We're on Dedicated.

Sam
BrightCart — SRE

[attachment: latency-trace-20260915.png]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Lee <sam@brightcart.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency starting ~08:45 PDT — can we get a standby plan?

Sam — thanks for the trace. We're standing up an internal bridge now. High level plan that I'm proposing (will iterate):

1) Immediate customer standby guidance (we'll send a short note you can post to your engineers) — short-term: reduce concurrency per client by 20% and enable request-level fast-fail at 1.5s.
2) Routing fallback: promote the compatible quantized model variant (q4b) in the same region for read-heavy flows; fallback for write-heavy flows to a lower sequence-length profile.
3) Protective soft-failover (circuit): if instance-level p95 > 1.2s for 3 consecutive minutes, route new sessions to the dedicated spill pool (we have warm spare capacity).
4) Product asks: need a quick decision from Product on enabling automatic spill routing for Dedicated customers (config toggle) vs a manual ops step.

Ben, Kim, Marissa — can SRE/Runtime confirm: is the warm spare pool fully warmed for BrightCart's model family? If not, what's the estimated warmup time and ETA to flip?

I'll draft a one-paragraph customer-ready standby note and share for approval.

—Rishi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:49:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency starting ~08:45 PDT — can we get a standby plan?

Rishi — joining bridge. Quick notes from runtime:
- Warm spare pool has q4b variant available but KV cache is cold for BrightCart's common prefixes; first 30s of traffic may see elevated tail.
- Warmup path: pre-fill KV cache using a targeted prefix replay (we can seed top 500 prefixes in ~2m if BrightCart gives us sample prompts).
- Autoscaler currently touching pool sizes; we'll pin spill pool to avoid autoscaler shrinking for next 1 hour.

Marissa: can we expose the "soft-failover circuit" toggle as an emergency flag in the console today? If not today, we need a runbook to execute manually (API call + routing policy).

Ben
Engineering (Runtime)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T10:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency starting ~08:45 PDT — can we get a standby plan?

On the product side:
- We do not have an automated "spill routing for Dedicated" toggle shipped. Minimum viable shipping path: a console flag + API param that flips routing from primary pool -> spill pool for customer_id. Scope: ~2 sprint work but we can do an emergency manual override via operations.
- Priorities/questions: do we want the toggle to be global (for all Dedicated) or per-customer? For BrightCart we should keep it per-customer.
- Roadmap ask: Add an in-console emergency soft-failover control and an audit log entry (product/backlog: RW-1984).

I will prepare a customer-ready note and a short ops runbook for manual execution.

Marissa
Head of Product — Redwood Console

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Lee <sam@brightcart.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Customer standby note: BrightCart — short mitigation steps (for your engs)

Sam — attaching a short plan you can paste to your SRE channel. We'll be on-call and can flip if you give the go.

Standby steps (short):
1) Reduce client concurrency to 80% of current for 30 minutes.
2) Apply request timeout 1.5s client-side.
3) If tail does not recover in 10 minutes, tell us to initiate the soft-failover circuit: we will route new sessions to the warm spare pool (q4b variant) and seed KV cache for top prefixes.

Ops notes: our manual runbook requires "emergency_route" API call with customer_id and routing_target; pre-seeded prefixes recommended. Attachment: standby_customer_note_v1.docx

Let us know if you want us to execute immediately; otherwise we'll wait for your authorization.

—Rishi

From: Samuel Lee <sam@brightcart.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightCart SRE Team <ops@brightcart.com>, Asha Raman <asha@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-09-16T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer standby note: BrightCart — short mitigation steps (for your engs)

Rishi — thanks. We briefed internal ops. Two quick asks before we give the go for the soft-failover: 
1) Can you confirm expected p95 after the spill routing warms (ballpark)?
2) Are there quality regressions we should expect from q4b on our checkout prompts? We can provide 200 sample prompts for seeding and QA.

If answers look ok we'll signal "go" and provide samples for pre-seed.

Sam

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Samuel Lee <sam@brightcart.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-16T18:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer standby note: BrightCart — short mitigation steps (for your engs)

Sam — quick answers:
- Expected p95 after warmup: ~650-800ms (ballpark) for checkout flows based on q4b perf profiles and seeded KV prefixes. We'll monitor for the first 10 minutes and report telemetry.
- Quality impact: q4b is quantized but within our acceptable QA thresholds for templated checkout prompts. There can be tokenization edge cases — we'll run your 200 samples through a quick evaluation and share top diffs.

If you approve, we'll execute the manual soft-failover, seed the prefixes you provide, and keep the spill pool pinned for 30 minutes.

Kim
Principal Product Engineer — Runtime Optimizations
